input.justification: User-controlled `bar` (from request.args.get) is concatenated directly into a file path (`fileName = f'{TESTFILES_DIR}/{bar}'`) which is then passed to `open()`. The only guard is a naive substring check `if '../' in bar`, which is an incomplete blacklist: it only catches the literal three-character sequence '../' and can be bypassed by alternate path-traversal techniques (e.g. backslash-based traversal '..\\', or other OS-specific separators, or by splitting the sequence across multiple characters that still resolve to a parent-directory traversal in some environments). The check does not canonicalize the path (no os.path.abspath/os.path.normpath + prefix check), so it does not reliably prevent directory traversal. Thus tainted data reaches the `open()` sink with insufficient sanitization, matching the classic Path Injection pattern.
missing_information: Exact OS/filesystem environment Benchmark runs on (affects whether backslash-based bypass is exploitable)
Whether werkzeug/Flask pre-normalizes query parameters in a way that would prevent alternate encodings from reaching the check unescaped
